title: IAM-broker grant document
description: The IAM-broker grant document, as defined in The Software Field Guide, issue #104: the supply-chain IAM-broker scope chapter's YAML — the broker's grants as data. The document declares the consumer identities the broker recognizes and every grant it issued: each grant names one principal, one component pinned by sha256 digest, an allowed action set, and an expiry. Judged at the broker gate against the component package manifest (the component gate's word, book issue #101), as a conformance gate — not an advisor: a grant whose component the manifest neither packages nor pins, a grant pinned at a digest the manifest never published, a wildcard or glob action, an undeclared principal, a duplicated grant, and an expired grant still on the books are all refused. The gate is honest about what it models: the action vocabulary is not modeled (any exact, non-metacharacter action name is allowed — the gate refuses broad scopes, not unfamiliar verbs), the expiry has no maximum horizon (only not in the past), and the security of the underlying identity infrastructure is the broker's word, not policy's. This schema mirrors the shape rules of the Rego validator (policies/broker); the validator additionally enforces the semantic rules a JSON schema cannot — reviewedOn a real calendar date not in the future and not older than 365 days, the digest well-formed and joined against the manifest, principals declared before they are granted, and the two drifts judged at the join.

version.description: The grant document's version. The grants are versioned like the components they consume.

reviewedOn.description: Date the grant document was last reviewed, YYYY-MM-DD. The validator flags reviews older than 365 days and dates in the future: grants nobody re-reads are grants nobody still vouches for.

owner.description: The team that owns the grant document. Grants without an owner are scope nobody maintains.

principals.description: The consumer identities the broker declares — the identities a grant may name. A grant naming an undeclared principal is refused; a grant naming no principal at all never reaches the join.

items.description: One consumer identity, by exact name.

grants.description: Every grant the broker issued. A broker that grants nothing brokers nothing; a grant nobody can read is a finding, never an ambiguous card.

principal.description: The consumer identity the grant is issued to, by exact name — one principal, one grant. The validator requires the principal to be declared in this document.

component.description: The component the grant consumes, by exact name. At the gate the name must resolve: the manifest packages the component or pins it as a dependency.

digest.description: The sha256 digest of the component the grant is pinned to. A grant for a component by name alone is a grant that can change under the broker; at the gate the pin must equal a digest the manifest publishes for that component.

actions.description: The grant's allowed action set: exact names. The wildcard action and any action carrying glob metacharacters are refused — a grant that can do anything is the scope the broker exists to prevent. The vocabulary is not modeled: any exact, non-metacharacter name is allowed.

items.description: One allowed action, by exact name.

expires.description: The date the grant expires, YYYY-MM-DD. Scope without a clock is scope forever; a grant expiring before today is a grant the broker never revoked. There is no maximum horizon — only the past is refused.
